A null person or one without the sheet: the "Error" box (line 0x657) and 0.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_position_aptitude(person, mask)` (`this` not used), called by update_player_training (0x8b1750, the position training complaint) and by set_position_training_rate (0x8b4450): the player's aptitude to learn a position or side: the average of the adaptability (person's +0x56) and the attributes the position needs (ratings 1 to 20 through 0x544380 over the sheet +0x61). \n Goalkeeper (1) +0x39, +0x2a and +0x35, over 4; defence (2, 4) +0x3e, +0x39 and +0x32, over 4; midfield and attack (8, 0x10, 0x20) +0x37, +0x32, +0x40 and +0x3f, over 5; 0x40 +0x33, +0x27, +0x40 and +0x36, over 5; 0x80 +0x30, over 2; 0x200 only the adaptability (in al, the upper bytes with the mask); 0x800 +0x3b, over 2 (truncated divisions). Any other mask: the "Error" box (line 0x945) and 0.

`TRAINING_SCHEDULE::set_type(slot, type)`: stores the schedule's slot and type and its five category levels from the type's mix. \n The slot (signed, as a dword) at +0, the type at +0x15 and the five category levels (+4..+8) by the type's mix (jump table 0x8b4f08): 1 general (25 in the first four), 2 to 5 one category at 50 and the others at 10, 6 goalkeepers (50 in the fifth, 0 in the third), 0 and 7 no training (all 0); outside 0..=7 (the −1 of the human's first slot) only the slot and the type. Called by set_default_schedules (0x8b3d40, 167 times at the start of the game) and by the training screens.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::set_default_schedules()`, called by the constructor (0x8b0ec0) in a new game (without training.dat): sets up the computer's seven schedules and the ten schedules of each of the 16 human managers, then gives the default names. \n The computer's seven schedules (0x9b bytes each from this; type k in slot k: the computer trains through slot 1, general, and slot 6, goalkeepers, according to the player's training entry) and, for each of the 16 human managers (person [0xae2364] − h − 1, 0x6e-byte record in [0xae23bc]), the ten schedules: slots 0 to 5 computed here (types −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4), 6 to 9 through 0x8b3930 (types 5, 6, 7, 7). At the end the default names (0x8b2230). Called by address (0x8b4e50 and 0x8b3930 in this batch).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_manager_schedule(manager, slot)`: returns the human manager's schedule for the slot (0..=9; outside that, 1): this + 0x9b × (slot + 10 × human + 7), human = [0xae2364] − id − 1. Outside the 16 human managers: the box (line 0x68f) and 0. Called by 0x8b3d40 (slots 6 to 9) and by the screens.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_coaching_factor(club, category)`, called by TRAINING_MANAGER::update_player_training (0x8b1750, five times per player in each training update; the value goes in as (factor − 100) / 5 into the weight of the progress roll): the coaching factor of a training category. \n A null club: 0. Without a manager (+0xcf) or with a computer manager (id below [0xae2364] − 16): 100 (eax carries the upper 16 bits of the manager pointer, as in the original). A human manager: his staff (0x8b4cd0, six 9-byte slots: id −1 is an empty slot, the category rating at +4 + category); with n coaches with a rating, the sum (16 bits) divided by the nth divisor and truncated (_ftol 0x945640), × 40/7 (0x970400) and truncated; below 50, 50. Hot on the computer branch: no counter there.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::get_coach_assignments(manager)`: returns the training staff table (six 9-byte slots) of one of the 16 human managers, at this + 0x652d + 54 × ([0xae2364] − id − 1). \n A null manager: the "Error" box (line 0xa20) and 0; outside the 16 human managers: the box (line 0xa2a) and 0.

`TRAINING_SCHEDULE::get_training_load()`: the schedule's load from its five category levels (+4..+8, signed) with fixed weights, up to 100. \n trunc(+8 × 0.5) − trunc(+4 × −1.3) − trunc(+7 × −0.5) − trunc(+6 × −0.5) − trunc(+5 × −0.5) (constants 0x968968, 0x96f878, 0x969540; _ftol 0x945640), in 16 bits; from 100 up, 100. Called by update_player_training (0x8b1750, the human club's player), by set_player_schedule (0x8b2250) and by reassign_squad_schedules (0x8b2470); it goes to the fitness sheet (Injury::set_training_load 0x62c660).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::apply_training_progress(person, d)`, called by update_player_training (0x8b1750, each player on each training update) and by 0x8b3640 and 0x8b37c0: adds each category's progress to the player's stored nibble, moving the category attributes, then handles the trained position or side. \n A null person: the "Error" box (line 0x4b3); without the sheet (+0x61): the box (line 0x4ba); an id from [0xae2364] on: nothing. With the player's 6-byte entry (this +0x651d + 6 × sheet id), each category with progress `d[k]` other than zero moves its step (progress_step over the stored nibble) on its sheet attributes (those from 1 to 20 by the step, those from −125 to 125 by six times the step; every two steps the attributes move) and stores the nibble plus `d[k]`: 3 (+4 high), 0 (+3 low), 2 (+4 low), 1 (+3 high) and 4 (+5 low). \n Then the position training (0x8b4b20): with the learning entry at 15 or more, the position or side of the mask goes to 20 (learnt); below that, it goes back to 1 (training stopped) if more than one position (+0xf..+0x15) or side (+0x17..+0x19) at 15 or more is still left. Hot: no counter.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::find_position_training(person, &first)`: finds the player's first entry in the sorted position training list and returns how many are his. \n A null person, the "Error" box (line 0x995); a null output, the box (line 0x99c); without the sheet (+0x61), the box (line 0x9a3): 0. Without flag 0x10 in +5 of the player's training entry (this +0x651d + 6 × sheet id), the position training mark: 0. Otherwise the binary search (0x946464, order 0x8b4e00) of the person's id in the position training list (this +0x6521, count +0x6525, 8-byte items); not found: 0; found: steps back to the person's first item, stores it in the output and returns how many consecutive ones are hers.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::has_fast_position_training(person)`, called by the people's daily update (game_daily_staff_update 0x5ce2d0): returns 1 if some item of the person's position training (0x8b4b20) has a learning rate (+7) above 50; otherwise 0.

`TRAINING_MANAGER::advance_week_counter(&day)`, every day from the day loop (game_main_day_loop 0x5cccd0, with the day of the year of the game date 0xae2c90): on a day that is a multiple of 7 (signed remainder), the training week (+0x688d, 16 bits) goes up by 1; update_player_training (0x8b1750) catches up each player with the missing weeks. Returns day / 7 (the caller does not read it).

`TRAINING_MANAGER::init_player_entries()`, called by the constructor (0x8b0ec0) in a new game: allocates the 6-byte training entry of every player sheet and puts goalkeepers on schedule 6 and the others on 1. \n Allocates (calloc 0x945501) the 6-byte training entries, one per player sheet ([0xae236c] sheets of 0x46 bytes in [0xae23c4], the sheet by its id +0), at this + 0x651d; without memory, the box (line 0x6e3) and it returns. In each entry it clears bit 0x20 of +5 and sets the schedule slot (+0): 6 (goalkeepers) with a goalkeeping rating (+0xf, signed) of 15 or more, otherwise 1 (general). Each player's first training update (0x8b1750, which only afterwards redoes the slot of the computer's players) and all of the human club's training use this slot.
